universal_lens: The Adaptability Index unifies continuous playstyle manifolds with discrete event topologies via mutual information. By mapping high-dimensional spatial coordinates to a shared entropy space, the framework quantifies structural dependencies between player movements and systemic game states without relying on Euclidean distance metrics. A mathematical framework for measuring player adaptability through information-theoretic entropy and positional entropy, integrating temporal and spatial player coordination data.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs the Kozachenko-Leonenko estimator to construct Bayesian posterior distributions over latent playstyle densities. Conformal inference bounds are established using k-nearest neighbor volumes, providing rigorous uncertainty quantification for out-of-distribution adaptability scores when projecting historical player data into novel tactical environments. Bayesian inference models player adaptability by computing mutual information between lineup configurations and positional entropy, enabling probabilistic predictions of performance variance.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the mutual information chain rule to decompose situational reasoning into conditional state transitions. By isolating the incremental information gained from ball possession versus pure spatial coordination, the engine dynamically updates real-time tactical priors as the underlying event topology shifts. Situational reasoning engine maps player state transitions via possession-based event sequences, capturing dynamic adaptation through real-time positional and lineup entropy changes.

primitives.name: Continuous Mutual Information Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Mutual information can also be written in the continuous case with integrals pp(xx, yy) = pp(xx)pp(yy) (6) ~~�~~ II(XX; YY) ≡� ff(xx, yy) log �<sup>ff(xx, yy)</sup> ddyyddxx xx∈XX,yy∈YY **2.2.
primitives.latex: I(X; Y) \equiv \int_{x \in X, y \in Y} f(x, y) \log \frac{f(x, y)}{f(x)f(y)} dy dx
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: X, Y: Continuous random variables (dimensionless state spaces); f(x,y): Joint probability density function (1/(unit_x * unit_y)); f(x), f(y): Marginal probability densities; I(X;Y): Mutual information (nats or bits).
primitives.assumptions: Playstyle variables contain continuous components; joint and marginal densities exist and are differentiable almost everywhere.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities occur if the joint density is supported on a lower-dimensional manifold where marginals vanish, causing the logarithmic ratio to diverge.

primitives.name: Kozachenko-Leonenko Entropy Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ff(xx) ff(xx) It is possible to directly estimate the entropy of a random variable using a k-nearest neighbor approach like the Kozachenko-Leonenko estimator[3] which is what's used in this work.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N: Number of samples (dimensionless count); k: Number of nearest neighbors (dimensionless integer); c_d: Volume of unit ball in d dimensions (length^d); \varepsilon_i: Distance to k-th nearest neighbor (length).
primitives.assumptions: Data points are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) drawn from an absolutely continuous distribution; metric space is well-defined.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Curse of dimensionality causes nearest-neighbor distances to converge to the radius of the entire support as dimensionality increases, rendering volume estimates meaningless.

layer2.mapping: Derives local phase-space density kernels for GSI's conformal prediction sets, allowing non-parametric boundary estimation of player adaptability clusters.

primitives.name: Local Probability Mass Approximation
primitives.verbatim_quote: This estimation begins with the approximation that the probability mass around a point is equal to a sufficiently small volume centered at that point multiplied by a ii constant probability density throughout the volume.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(\varepsilon_i): Probability mass within radius (dimensionless); f(x_i): Probability density at point x_i (1/length^d); V_d: Volume of unit hypersphere (dimensionless geometric constant); \varepsilon_i: Radius to k-th neighbor (length); d: Dimensionality (integer).
primitives.assumptions: Probability density function is locally constant within the infinitesimal neighborhood defined by the k-th nearest neighbor.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails near sharp boundaries of the support or highly multimodal distributions where the local density assumption is violated by rapid gradients.

primitives.name: Mutual Information Chain Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: The mutual information "chain-rule", proven in Appendix B, can separate the effects of mutual information between the components of the playstyle joint random variable.
primitives.latex: I(L; B, C) = I(L; B) + I(L; C | B)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L: Lineup random variable (categorical/discrete); B: Ball possession Boolean (binary); C: Player coordinates (continuous vector); I: Mutual information (nats/bits).
primitives.assumptions: Random variables form a valid joint probability space; conditional mutual information is well-defined given the realization of B.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates if B deterministically dictates C (perfect collinearity), making the conditional term zero and masking nuanced spatial adaptations.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's hierarchical state machine, separating baseline lineup constraints from dynamic, possession-dependent spatial adjustments.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of conditional spatial information I(L;C|B) to unconditional spatial information I(L;C).

primitives.breakdown_regime: When N_off < 5 or players are not entirely on offensive side of court.

primitives.name: Ball Possession Boolean
primitives.verbatim_quote: For any frame, if the ball is within a 3-foot radius in the x-y plane and the ball is no higher than 3 feet above the player's z-coordinates, then the player is in possession of the ball.

primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball distance exceeds 3 feet or vertical separation exceeds 3 feet.
